messages:
alice_acme: Hey — hitting intermittent failures on the embeddings endpoint since this morning. Our service sends batches of vectors to POST /v1/embeddings and ~1 in 10 calls now returns HTTP 400 with message "dimension mismatch". When it succeeds the vectors are length 1024, when it errors sometimes the server says expected 1024 got 1536. No code changes on our side. p95 latency also spiked from ~120ms to ~1.2s. Repro steps below. Any idea?

alice_acme: Repro curl (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"vector-large-v2","input":[ [0.1,0.2,...(1024 numbers)...], ...(batch of 64) ]}'
```

alice_acme: Response when failing: `{"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536"}`. Request ID header returned: `x-request-id: trc_acme_7e2b`.

sara_support: Hey @alice_acme — thanks for the report and repro. Sorry for the interruption. A few quick checks: can you confirm all 64 vectors in your batch are the same length on the client before send? Also did you switch models recently (or are some callers still sending `vector-xlarge` while others send `vector-large-v2`)?

alice_acme: We never mix models intentionally. The batch is assembled from a queued stream from different downstream workers though — I'll double-check that they don't send an older model param.

sara_support: Also can you paste the full response headers from the failed request (we need the `x-request-id` and `x-model-version` headers if present). That helps us map to traces on our side.

alice_acme: Header dump: `x-request-id: trc_acme_7e2b`, `x-model: vector-large-v2`, `x-model-version: v2.3.1`, `x-server-node: node-17`

james_prodeng: Thanks — I pulled the trace with that id. Quick summary: some batches were coalesced by the gateway batcher and contained inputs that originated from two different client calls; one of those calls had been routed to `vector-large-v2` v2.3.1 and the other to `vector-xlarge` v1.9.0 (different returned embedding dims). Our batcher used the first model in the batch to pick a kernel and then the backend validated dims and rejected the batch once it saw mismatch.

james_prodeng: We should have returned a clearer error earlier; currently it surfaces as a generic "dimension mismatch". We're tracking a better error code like `400: mixed-model-batch` with metadata.

alice_acme: Ok that matches what we suspected — we have a few workers that haven't been rolled to the new SDK pinned to v2.3.1. What's the recommended mitigation while we rollout?

liam_infra: Short-term options: 1) disable request coalescing for your org (we can toggle a routing flag for your org) — that prevents cross-request batch composition but reduces throughput. 2) set `batching.max_batch_size=1` in your request header or SDK config to avoid mixing at the gateway. 3) pin model version per request (include `model_version: v2.3.1`) so our router won't mix incompatible variants.

liam_infra: I can flip the org-level toggle for 24 hours while you finish the rollout. Which do you prefer?

alice_acme: We'll take the toggle for 24h while we finish the rollout. Also we need to understand why p95 latency ballooned — is that related?

james_prodeng: The trace shows increased `batch_wait_ms` during the period because the coalescer waited longer to reach target batch sizes (some requests were rejected and retried), plus one backend node showed transient GC spikes increasing compute_ms. That combined pushed p95 up.

sara_support: To help you monitor, here are where to look in Console: Observability -> Routes -> `embeddings.vectorize` -> switch to Request list. Click the failing request id to see timeline slices: `queue_wait_ms`, `batch_wait_ms`, `compute_ms`, `encode_ms`, `network_ms`. We also instrument tokenization time under `encode_ms` for models that do client-side pre-tokenization.

sara_support: You can also query traces directly via our traces UI: https://console.redwood.example/observability/traces/trc_acme_7e2b (we've loaded the trace for you).

obs-bot: trace link: https://tracing.redwood.example/trace/trc_acme_7e2b — timeline shows: queue_wait=12ms, batch_wait=540ms, compute=280ms, encode=40ms, network=48ms. Top span indicates `batch_coalescer` merged two model variants.

alice_acme: Thanks, that timeline is helpful. Can you share the raw trace or the log lines so we can correlate with our client logs?

james_prodeng: Pasting redacted trace excerpt and log lines (server side):
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] trc_acme_7e2b batch_coalescer: coalesced 2 requests sizes=[32,32] models=[vector-large-v2:v2.3.1, vector-xlarge:v1.9.0]
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] trc_acme_7e2b gateway: forwarded batch->backend node-17 kernel=optimized-fp16
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] trc_acme_7e2b backend node-17: validation failed: expected dim=1024 got=1536 -> responded 400 dimension mismatch
```

james_prodeng: For full raw logs I can create a redacted bundle and share privately — need your approval to include request payloads.

alice_acme: Approve — share bundle with support. Also can you add a dashboard panel for our team showing `fraction of failed batches due to mixed-model` (if you can surface that) and `batch_wait_ms` p50/p95? We'll watch during rollout.

liam_infra: Yes — I'll add two panels under your org's Observability > Dashboards > Acme-Embed-Health: (1) Error breakdown by failure_type (mixed_model, validation, backend_error) (2) Embeddings route latency breakdown (queue/batch/compute/network) p50/p95. ETA ~ 90 minutes.

sara_support: Done on the org toggle — coalescing disabled for `acme.com` for 24h. Also added an alert that fires if `mixed_model` failures > 0.5% over 5m.

alice_acme: Confirmed — our error rate dropped to 0 immediately after the toggle. Thanks! We'll finish the rollout in the next hour and then you can re-enable coalescing.

james_prodeng: Follow-up: we'll push a small change to the gateway to validate model compatibility earlier and return `400 mixed-model-batch` with `x-batch-details` header so clients get a clearer reason (and clients can decide to retry single-request). That will go out in the next patch release.

liam_infra: I'll also add a trace tag `batch_model_list` so traces explicitly list model ids involved in a batch — should make debugging faster.

alice_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Two action items for us: (1) finish pinning SDKs to v2.3.1, (2) add a pre-send client check to assert all vectors in a batch have the same length and model param. We'll close once rollout done.

sara_support: Great — ping us when you're ready and we'll re-enable coalescing and monitor metrics. :thumbsup:
